newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan interbank rate ends down, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan interbank rate ends down, seen rising.

text.p: Taiwan's interbank rate closed slightly lower on Monday, but dealers said the rate faced rising pressure on Tuesday after the central bank's move to mop up liquidity in the banking system.
The overnight interbank rate closed at 6.588 percent against Saturday's 6.594 finish -- outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but far below the double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper rose to 6.50-6.75 percent against 6.25-6.50.
The central bank on Monday issued T$11 billion negotiable certificates of deposit at an average yield of 6.753 percent.
Dealers said market sentiment has turned cautious after the central bank's move.
The bond market was listless as many traders adopted a wait-and-see attitude. The 10-year 86/4 bond yield was traded in a 5.8900-8980 range.
